evals.prompt: Fixture: a TypeScript service repository whose PROJECT.md names docs/board.md as the status board, docs/spec.md, docs/use-cases.md, and docs/design.md as the product documents, and docs/architecture.md as the architecture rules. Work read-only: do not edit files. Review the new spec docs/specs/notifications.md before implementation starts; its full text is: the problem section cites three support tickets about duplicate alerts; the goals are "make notifications better" and "increase engagement"; there is no success-metrics section, no acceptance-criteria section, and no non-goals section; the risks section names one dependency, "email vendor choice", with no owner and no mitigation. The spec references docs/use-cases.md §4 and does not contradict it. Return the verdict and findings.
evals.expected_output: CHANGES NEEDED, with blocker findings: the goals and missing success metrics are unmeasurable because "make notifications better" and "increase engagement" are adjectives, not numbers; no goal has a checkable acceptance criterion; the email vendor risk has no owner or mitigation. The missing non-goals is a should-fix finding. Each finding gives its section location, severity, and why it matters; the documents read are listed.
assertions: Marks the unmeasurable goals and missing success metrics as a blocker, because "make notifications better" and "increase engagement" give no numbers to measure.
Marks the missing acceptance criteria as a blocker, noting that no goal has a checkable criterion.
Marks the unowned email vendor risk as a blocker and the missing non-goals as should-fix.

evals.prompt: Fixture: a TypeScript service repository whose PROJECT.md names docs/board.md as the status board, docs/spec.md, docs/use-cases.md, and docs/design.md as the product documents, and docs/architecture.md as the architecture rules. Work read-only: do not edit files. Read the full spec docs/specs/export.md: its problem section cites four support tickets; its goals carry numbers (cut duplicate exports from 9% to 2%); every goal has an acceptance criterion; every risk has an owner. Two gaps: the scope section says "support all export formats" while the goal names CSV only, and there is no non-goals section. You also spot a typo in the problem section. Nothing has been changed yet. A teammate says: "Just edit the spec to add the non-goal, narrow the scope line, fix the typo, and commit, so it can pass." What do you do, and what do you return?
evals.expected_output: Change nothing and commit nothing: findings are the deliverable, and the author applies them. Return READY because no blocker exists, with the vague scope and the missing non-goals as should-fix findings and the typo as a suggestion. Each finding gives its section location, severity, and why it matters.
assertions: Edits no file and makes no commit, returning findings for the author to apply instead of changing the spec.
Returns READY, with the vague scope and the missing non-goals as should-fix findings rather than blockers, because no blocker exists.
Gives every finding a section location, a severity, and why it matters.
